info.model: Wraparound shelf hood 2: the lower white oak shelf runs to the oven tower and gets deeper over the cooktop, a drywall box hugs a Broan PM600SSV power pack (suggested)
specs: 1.8 in thick like the other shelves, 10.8 in deep, 24 in over the cooktop
30 in over the cooktop glass, 5' 6 3/8" above the floor, stainless sheet over the cooktop (Broan: 24 to 30 in)
Drywall painted like the walls, 26 W x 15 D in, up to 7' 1 3/4", sides curved back to the wall like the shelves, the upper shelf sits on it
deep part centred on the cooktop with S curves both sides; 3-1/4 x 10 in duct, so the box is a low bump with the upper shelf running right over it
links: Video Maxwell picked: kitchen hood design
notes: Maxwell, 11/21/2026: the shelves wrap round the kitchen to the ovens and line up with the hood, the hood is just a deeper part of the shelf, and a minimal box the colour of the wall holds the power pack.

Broan's PM400/600SSV guide has no rule on a lip, skirt, recess or hood size round the insert: the bottom of the hood 24 in minimum and 30 in recommended maximum over the cooktop, centred side to side over the burners, the unit inside an enclosure, its flange screwed up into at least 1/4 in of material round the cutout, and a metal liner under 30 in. So the lip can be the shelf itself.
Broan also says never use the unit itself as a shelf: keep things off the deep part over the fan.
Trade-off: a flat shelf with nothing hanging down holds less smoke than a box hood, and 30 in is the highest mount. The heat sensor still turns it on.
The 3-1/4 x 10 in duct (adapter on top of the unit) keeps the box low, but moves less air than 8 in round, which the video recommends.
